record.paper_title: Problems and Conjectures in Matrix and Operator Inequalities
record.original_question: Let X and Y be complex m×n matrices, let f:R_+→R_+ be concave with f(0)=0, and let σ_i(·) denote singular values in nonincreasing order. For each k≤min(m,n), does the stronger majorization-style inequality ∑_{i=1}^k |f(σ_i(X))-f(σ_i(Y))| ≤ ∑_{i=1}^k f(σ_i(X-Y)) always hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X, Y \in M_{m,n}(\mathbb{C})$ be complex $m \times n$ matrices, and for a matrix $A$ let $\sigma_1(A) \ge \sigma_2(A) \ge \cdots \ge \sigma_{\min(m,n)}(A) \ge 0$ denote its singular values arranged in nonincreasing order. Let $f : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ be a concave function with $f(0) = 0$. Prove or disprove: for every integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le \min(m,n)$,
$$\sum_{i=1}^{k} \bigl| f(\sigma_i(X)) - f(\sigma_i(Y)) \bigr| \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^{k} f(\sigma_i(X-Y)).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (Miao's conjecture) was resolved affirmatively. A proof was given by Audenaert (arXiv:1410.4941, "A generalisation of Mirsky's singular value inequalities"), which establishes a stronger statement: for any concave f:R_+→R_+ with f(0)=0 and any increasing sequence of indices i_1<...<i_m, the sum ∑|f(σ_{i_k}(X))−f(σ_{i_k}(Y))| is bounded by ∑_{k=1}^m f(σ_k(X−Y)). Foucart's "Concave Mirsky Inequality and Low-Rank Recovery" (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl., 2018) gives an alternative proof and applications.

status_evidence.title: A generalisation of Mirsky's singular value inequalities (Audenaert)
status_evidence.snippet: Their f-version is essentially the set of inequalities conjectured by W. Miao... We therefore have solved this conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Miao's conjecture is proved (and generalized to arbitrary increasing index sets).

status_evidence.title: Concave Mirsky Inequality and Low-Rank Recovery (Foucart)
status_evidence.snippet: We propose a simple proof of a generalized Mirsky inequality comparing the differences of singular values of two matrices with the singular values of their difference.
status_evidence.claim: An independent proof of the concave Mirsky/Miao inequality is given.
